column1: # Every defect seen in a capture, and what happened to it.
#   open      seen and reproduced, not repaired -- defect_gate.py fails on this
#   fixed     repaired; evidence names the capture that shows it repaired
#   refuted   re-measured, the original report was wrong; note says how
#   accepted  the owner said in writing to ship it as it is
# Writing a row here is what makes an unrepaired defect fail a gate instead of
# sitting in a paragraph nobody re-reads.  Add the row when you SEE it, not
# when you get around to it.

column6: WRONG as reported. The host re-resolves every subscription by name whenever the tree instance changes and raises UNBOUND; App_PluginLayoutTick passes instance 0 for the whole login screen, so a bound watch is back to PENDING before the poll would have spoken. What was missing was the test, and a testbed that retired a node identity on unbind instead of handing the same ref back

REAL. PORCELAIN_INPUT_SCREEN was an enumerator nothing ever raised, so a description that watches no element (AT_CANVAS, a fixed corner) was never re-asked at a transition. Masked on the usual path because a logout unbinds every element. Porcelain now reads core.screen once per fence and stamps the input on a change

column6: REAL, and the defect was in the CAPTURE rather than in the plugin. The pair was shot at 21:31 and 22:02 with the 83c75b410 binary; 190648c80 (a tile border is the cache's thickness, and 0 is no border) landed at 22:32 and 74fc1f13f (the parked pointer stopped costing a session) at 22:35, and neither re-took it -- so two repaired bugs went on being photographed as live and were re-reported off the picture. Re-taken with a byte-identical plugins.ini, preferences.ini and drive, only the binary differing: unblended 0xBEBA6E over the frame 389 -> 0, the tile interior px(293,200) (105,103,78) both times so the wash survived, the control's same px (74,72,67) both times, and pure white in the viewport band y150..220 -- the teardown banner's text -- 649 -> 0. An A/A pair moves nothing in the tile band, so the entity and minimap deltas between shot and control are run-to-run and only the tile is the plugin's

the tile wash paints OVER the entity standing on the tile. Group 5 is flags=10, which carries no ALWAYS_ON_TOP bit, yet at 8x over x310..360 y180..215 the npc's boots are the olive wash in the shot and dark purple in the control. Seen in the re-taken capture above and written down here rather than left in a commit message; named as out of scope by 190648c80 and still is -- the overlay stage is a 2D pass after the whole scene, so the only place a marker can sort UNDER an entity is the painter's ground-decor step, which needs a scene-integrated ground primitive and not a change to this plugin
